newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index put on 153.86 points, or 1.26 percent, to 12,346.03 in the first 10 minutes of trade on Wednesday morning, rebounding after losing ground over the last four trading days, brokers said.
"A surge in the futures is certainly a contributing factor," said one broker with a large European house.

The Hang Seng Index October futures contract put on 105 points to 12,335, to trade at a slight premium to the cash market. The November contract followed, gaining 102 points to 12,340. The October contract expires on Wednesday.
Brokers, however, said the underlying factor was the strength seen in the U.S. bond market in reaction to market-friendly economic data released on Tuesday.
"The market's up on the big move in the U.S. bond market," said Angus Shillington, institutional sales manager at Asia Equity.

The U.S. long bond rallied 2-4/32 overnight, pushing its yield down to 6.68 percent after third-quarter Employee Cost Index which showed the index rising only 0.6 percent, lower than forecast and suggesting that the U.S. interest rates will remain at current levels following the U.S. presidential election, brokers said.
"Some people are even saying there could be decrease in rates later in the year, a positive point for Hong Kong," said the European broker.
Technical analysts said the market's short term indicators still showed some near-term weakness, but longer term indicators were more positive, said one analyst.

The index heavyweights led the market, supporting brokers views that trade was linked to futures market activity. The commercial and industrial sector, which had been sold off in the market's previous four-day consolidation, led the market up in early trade. Properties were the next best performing.

Among the trading hongs, Swire Pacific gained HK$0.75 To HK$68.75, and CITIC Pacific put on HK$0.60 to HK$37.20. Properties favourites Sun Hung Kai Properties and Henderson Land added HK$1.50 and HK$1.00 to HK$86.25 and HK68.50 respectively.
HSBC Holdings added HK$1.50 to HK$156.00 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$1.50 to HK$91.25.
